library_preparation_preflight.summary: Avro 1.12.2 added ClassSecurityValidator, which rejects schema-driven class resolution (ReflectData/SpecificData getClassProp/getClass) for any class not explicitly trusted; the generated test's own POJOs now throw SecurityException unless the test package is added to org.apache.avro.SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES (or SERIALIZABLE_CLASSES).
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Reproduced locally: `env GVM_TCK_LV=1.12.2 ./gradlew clean javaTest -Pcoordinates=org.apache.avro:avro:1.12.1` fails 4 tests with `java.lang.SecurityException: Forbidden <TestClass>! This class is not trusted to be included in Avro schemas.` (thrown from org.apache.avro.util.ClassSecurityValidator via ReflectData.getClassProp / SpecificData.getClass). This is a new deny-by-default allowlist in 1.12.2, not a Native Image issue. Generated tests must add the test package to the trust list, e.g. in build.gradle's `test` task: `systemProperty 'org.apache.avro.SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES', 'org_apache_avro.avro'` (or `org.apache.avro.SERIALIZABLE_CLASSES` for a narrower per-class allowlist, or call `ClassSecurityValidator.setGlobal(...)`/pass a custom predicate in test code). Apply this only to the generated test module's own package — do not trust `org.apache.avro` or wildcard packages.
risks: If the fix instead widens ClassSecurityValidator trust broadly (e.g. all packages) rather than scoping to the test's own package, it would defeat the point of the security hardening being tested/exercised — keep the trust list scoped to the generated test package only.
